subject: pathology
title: Lysosomal and glycogen storage disorders

steps.tx: **Lysosomal storage disorders** follow inherited enzyme deficiencies that allow undegraded substrates to accumulate inside lysosomes over time. Stored material progressively enlarges the liver, spleen, brain or muscle depending on which substrate cannot be broken down. Most disorders inherit recessively, so carrier parents remain healthy while an affected child receives two faulty copies. **Enzyme replacement**, substrate reduction and stem cell therapy modify several types when treatment starts before irreversible damage occurs.
steps.say: Missing lysosomal enzymes allow undegraded material to accumulate inside cells and enlarge organs over many years. Recessive inheritance hides the defect in healthy carrier parents who pass faulty copies to their children unknowingly. Early enzyme replacement prevents permanent damage effectively in several disorders, so timing of diagnosis changes outcome greatly.

steps.tx: **Gaucher disease** lacks glucocerebrosidase and stores glucocerebroside inside macrophages that fill the spleen, liver and bone marrow. Those macrophages become **Gaucher cells** with crumpled tissue paper cytoplasm that examiners expect you to recognise on microscopy. Massive splenomegaly, cytopenias, bone pain and **Erlenmeyer flask deformity** of the femur follow visceral and marrow packing. Type 1 disease usually spares neurons, and enzyme replacement reverses visceral and blood features dramatically.
steps.say: Gaucher macrophages fill the spleen and marrow because stored lipid cannot break down without its enzyme present. Their cytoplasm looks like crumpled tissue paper, and bones deform into flask shapes after marrow expansion over years. Enzyme replacement reverses blood and organ disease dramatically when treatment starts before permanent skeletal damage occurs.

right.title: Tay Sachs disease
points: Cherry red spot, developmental regression, no organomegaly

steps.tx: The marrow is packed with large **Gaucher macrophages** whose pale cytoplasm shows fine wrinkles described as **crumpled tissue paper cytoplasm**. These storage cells crowd out normal marrow and mirror the splenic and hepatic packing that causes cytopenias and organ enlargement. Recognising Gaucher cells matters because it points directly to **glucocerebrosidase deficiency** and to enzyme replacement that reverses visceral disease. In the exam, crumpled tissue paper macrophages should immediately raise Gaucher disease.
steps.say: This marrow contains large storage macrophages with wrinkled cytoplasm that resembles crumpled tissue paper under the microscope. Those Gaucher cells crowd the marrow and enlarge the spleen because undegraded lipid accumulates inside macrophages everywhere. Recognition matters greatly because enzyme replacement reverses visceral disease when treatment starts before permanent damage develops.

vis.alt: Marrow packed with large Gaucher macrophages showing crumpled tissue paper cytoplasm.
vis.caption: Gaucher macrophages with crumpled tissue paper cytoplasm. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Tay Sachs disease** lacks hexosaminidase A and stores GM2 ganglioside inside neurons throughout the developing nervous system. Infants regress developmentally with exaggerated startle, blindness from a **cherry red macular spot** and death during childhood in classic disease. The liver and spleen do not enlarge, which separates Tay Sachs disease from many other storage disorders at the bedside. **Niemann Pick disease** instead stores sphingomyelin and combines organomegaly with neurodegeneration in affected infants.
steps.say: Tay Sachs disease stores ganglioside only inside neurons, so infants regress and develop a cherry red spot without organ enlargement. Niemann Pick disease adds liver and spleen enlargement because sphingomyelin accumulates in visceral macrophages as well as neurons. Organ size separates these disorders quickly at the bedside and appears repeatedly in examination questions for infants.

vis.alt: Comparison of Tay-Sachs (cherry-red macula, no organomegaly) and Niemann-Pick (hepatosplenomegaly) in infants.
vis.caption: Tay-Sachs (cherry-red spot) vs. Niemann-Pick (organomegaly) at the bedside

steps.tx: **Mucopolysaccharidoses** store glycosaminoglycans and cause coarse facial features, stiff joints, dysostosis and progressive intellectual decline in affected children. **Hurler syndrome** follows alpha L iduronidase deficiency and clouds the cornea as stored material deposits inside ocular tissue. **Hunter syndrome** is X linked and spares the cornea, which gives the favourite distinguishing pair between these two syndromes. Enzyme replacement and transplant improve somatic features more than established brain injury once damage has occurred.
steps.say: Hurler syndrome stores glycosaminoglycans and clouds the cornea while coarsening facial features during early childhood development. Hunter syndrome is X linked and keeps corneas clear, which separates the two syndromes in examination questions reliably. Early treatment protects the body more than the brain because established neuronal injury reverses poorly with therapy.

steps.tx: **Glycogen storage diseases** block glycogen breakdown at different steps and present through liver, muscle or heart depending on the enzyme. **Von Gierke disease** lacks glucose 6 phosphatase and causes fasting hypoglycaemia with a huge liver and lactic acidosis in infants. **Pompe disease** lacks acid maltase inside lysosomes and causes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with weak muscles in affected infants. **McArdle disease** lacks muscle phosphorylase and causes exercise cramps with a second wind phenomenon and myoglobinuria.
steps.say: Von Gierke disease prevents glucose release during fasting, so infants develop low sugar with a huge liver. Pompe disease weakens heart and skeletal muscle because its missing enzyme works inside lysosomes in both tissues. McArdle disease cramps exercising muscle severely, then improves through a second wind as other fuels arrive.
